title: Full AES-256 key recovery over a related-key-pair pool, BKN 2009 encryption-only TA variant

target.description: Standard full AES-256 key recovery using the pair-scanning first step and Section 4.2's alternative triangulation-based key completion, without a chosen-ciphertext oracle.

key_budget.note: The alternative changes only the second step; its first step retains the outer scan over 2^35 related-key pairs. The source does not specify a corresponding distinct-key total.

setting.key_relation: Each tested pair uses K and K XOR DeltaK with the fixed Appendix A master-key difference; a successful first step identifies a pair satisfying the weak key-schedule condition.
setting.key_population: A key from a qualifying weak related-key pair found among 2^35 tested candidate pairs; weak-pair incidence is estimated as 2^-35, not asserted for every designated key.
setting.plaintext_model: Chosen-plaintext structures for the first-stage pair scan; retained plaintext/ciphertext information is used for offline key-guess checking.
assumptions: The attacker has encryption access for the tested pair pool; decryption access is not assumed.
The first stage supplies 80 recovered key bits, combined with the 35 bits constrained by the weak key-schedule trail.
The key-schedule triangulation algorithm supplies 17 free bytes and the remaining admissible-value choices for the source's 2^141 assignment enumeration.

time.reported: 2^141 dominant key-assignment enumeration, after a 2^131 first-stage scan
time.note: Section 4.2 p.244 counts 2^(17*8+5)=2^141 possible assignments for the encryption-only completion. The preceding pair scan costs 2^131; it does not multiply the completion by 2^35 because completion follows a successful first-stage recovery. No exact full-AES-equivalent conversion is asserted.

data.note: Editorial arithmetic from the unchanged first stage: 2^35 tested pairs times 2^31 repetitions times two 2^64-text structures. The TA alternative is offline key completion and does not use the chosen-ciphertext pairs of the other variant.

memory.note: The first step alone is stated to use 2^64 memory; Table 1 summarizes key recovery with 2^65. The paper does not separately give peak storage for this alternative TA completion, so the encryption/decryption variant's overall memory is not silently copied.

preprocessing.note: The paper describes running triangulation on the key schedule but does not give a separate reusable preprocessing budget for this alternative; the pair scan remains included in attack time and data.

success.description: No numerical full-master-key recovery success is supplied. Testing2^35 related-key pairs uses a mean incidence, not a proved pool-hit probability; no independence or Poisson acquisition model is imposed. The first stage expects four right pairs,2^31 wrong pairs and2^47 random80-bit votes. The CPA triangulation variant enumerates2^141 admissible assignments; it does not use the CCA second-stage2^-87 trail/48-bit filter. Enumeration costs are not a success measurement. Expected counts are not converted into primary probabilities.

components.description: Section4.1: five key-schedule transitions each2^-7 give mean weak-pair incidence2^-35 in the source key model. This is not the probability that a2^35-pair pool contains a qualifying pair; independence between tested pairs is not established.
Section4.2 first step: remaining state-trail probability after the structured first two rounds, conditional on an actual qualifying key pair.

Section4.2: source assigns2^(64-93)=2^-29 to a structure producing a right pair. Retain this as its local first-moment approximation;2^31 repetitions give mean four, not an independently established end-to-end success distribution.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Local pair filters, conditional trails, weak-pair incidence and expected counts keep their own experiment; correlation is not a decision probability. Existing conflicts, resources, targets, settings and full-audit gates remain unchanged.

evidence.locator: Section 4.1 p.242; Section 4.2 First step pp.242-243; p.244, paragraph headed 'Second step with TA'.
evidence.interpretation: The alternative is expressly introduced to avoid chosen-ciphertext access. It combines the first-stage recovered bits and weak-key constraints through a key-schedule-only triangulation step, followed by 2^141 assignments. The unchanged first-stage pair scan is retained.

evidence.locator: CRYPTO proceedings PDF12–14 / printed242–244 Sections4.1–4.2 and Figure4; PDF3 Table1 distinguishes weak-pair and pool costs.
evidence.interpretation: No numerical full-master-key recovery success is supplied. Testing2^35 related-key pairs uses a mean incidence, not a proved pool-hit probability; no independence or Poisson acquisition model is imposed. The first stage expects four right pairs,2^31 wrong pairs and2^47 random80-bit votes. limitations: The selected goal is recovery of a key belonging to a qualifying pair from the pool, not arbitrary designated-key recovery.
The 2^141 figure counts source-native key-assignment enumeration and is not normalized to an exact number of complete AES-256 encryptions.
Separate peak memory and preprocessing for the TA variant are not reported.
No independent implementation or attack-cost reproduction was performed.
